claim_ceiling: This is an exact-rank benchmark for a deliberately simplified common-rate pathway model. AFEX raw data remain un-ingested. AM colonisation, root morphology, phosphatase and tissue nutrient concentration are proxies/traits, not source-specific nutrient-transfer fluxes. No AFEX pathway partition or fungal carbon cost is established.

unknown_parameters.meaning: direct inorganic nutrient uptake rate per uncolonised root fraction
mycorrhizal inorganic nutrient uptake rate per colonised root fraction
mycorrhizal organic nutrient acquisition rate per colonised root fraction
host carbon allocation cost associated with fungal symbiosis
unknown_parameters.unit: synthetic carbon cost units per plot-period

observation_operator.model_assumption: constant pathway coefficients shared across synthetic plots; AM colonisation fraction is treated as known covariate; total uptake is observed as a sum of the three nutrient pathways
observation_operator.carbon_cost_column: The total nutrient-uptake measurement contains no direct observation of host-to-fungal carbon allocation; coefficient is zero.
observation_operator.colonisation_semantics: AM colonisation fraction is a covariate in the observation operator, not itself an equation measuring pathway flux.

afex_current_observations.support: 0-10 and 10-30 cm; February 2018; plot/depth community means
0-10 and 10-30 cm; February 2018; potential enzyme assay
afex_current_observations.role: biochemical acquisition proxy, not realized P flux

cases.expected_conclusion: No direct pathway rate is structurally identified from the current trait-only observation set.
Direct-root rate and aggregate fungal contribution can be separated under the shared-rate assumption, but fungal inorganic and organic contributions remain aliased; carbon cost is unobserved.
The inorganic fungal component is source-resolved; carbon allocation cost remains unobserved.
All four parameters are structurally identified within the simplified shared-rate model; practical identifiability and ecological validity still require independent assessment.
